proposals.before: When Liu Chong of Bingzhou marched south, Tong was sent under Wang Yanchao of Hezhong to intercept him by way of Jinzhou; the force was beaten at Gaoping.
proposals.after: When Liu Chong of Bingzhou marched south, Tong was sent under Wang Yanchao of Hezhong to intercept him by way of Jinzhou; they defeated him at Gaoping.
proposals.reason: Chinese 擊之，敗於高平 after an ordered strike most naturally means they defeated the enemy at Gaoping; Zhou historically won Gaoping in 954, so 'the force was beaten' reverses the outcome.

proposals.before: Liu Chong of Bingzhou invaded southward. Tong was ordered to assist Wang Yanchao of Hezhong in striking him along the Jinzhou route, but they were defeated at Gaoping.
proposals.after: Liu Chong of Bingzhou invaded southward. Tong was ordered to assist Wang Yanchao of Hezhong in striking him along the Jinzhou route, and they defeated him at Gaoping.
proposals.reason: Literal 'but they were defeated' reverses 敗於高平 in this campaign context; the clause records Zhou success at Gaoping.

proposals.before: When Emperor Gong succeeded, Tong was transferred to garrison Yanzhou.
proposals.after: When Emperor Gong succeeded, Tong was transferred to garrison Yunzhou.
proposals.reason: Chinese 鄆州 is Yunzhou (modern Dongping area), not Yanzhou 兗州; the idiomatic rendering misidentifies the prefecture.

proposals.before: When Emperor Gong succeeded, Tong was transferred to garrison Yanzhou.
proposals.after: When Emperor Gong succeeded, Tong was transferred to garrison Yunzhou.
proposals.reason: Literal likewise renders 鄆州 as Yanzhou; correct place-name is Yunzhou.

proposals.before: Murong Yanhao and Wang Quanbin were sent by the eastern route to join Shouxin. With the inspector Li Chongju they routed Yun at Changping and took three thousand heads.
proposals.after: Murong Yanzhao and Wang Quanbin were sent by the eastern route to join Shouxin. With the inspector Li Chongju they routed Yun at Changping and took three thousand heads.
proposals.reason: Chinese 慕容延釗 is Murong Yanzhao (釗), not Yanhao; the idiomatic spelling misreads the given name.

proposals.before: That evening he feasted his officers with Shoujie present and appointed him training commissioner of Shan;
proposals.after: That evening he feasted his officers with Shoujie present and appointed him training commissioner of Shanzhou;
proposals.reason: 單州 is Shanzhou; truncating to 'Shan' obscures the prefecture name.

decisions.reason: The clause records Liu Chong's defeat at Gaoping. Reading it as a defeat of Tong and Wang Yanchao reverses the documented result and breaks the object continuity from 擊之.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 出晉州道擊之，敗於高平

decisions.reason: The literal field makes the same reversal. Tong and Wang Yanchao were sent to attack Liu Chong, whose forces were defeated at Gaoping.
The source has 鄆州, Yunzhou. Yanzhou would be 姚州 or 兌州 and names a different prefecture.
The literal field repeats the same place-name error; 鄆州 must be rendered Yunzhou here.
慕容延釗 is Murong Yanzhao. Yanhao is a mistranscription of the final character and is not an attested alternate name.

decisions.after: That day he feasted his officers with Shoujie present and appointed him training commissioner of Shanzhou;
decisions.reason: 單州 is the prefecture name Shanzhou, so the bare form 'Shan' obscures the territorial command. The revision also restores 是日 as 'that day,' correcting the unsupported 'that evening.'

sourceWitness.excerpt: 是日宴從官…以為單州團練使

claimRetractions.reason: Murong Yanhao was copied from the mistranslated English and conflicts with both the Chinese name and the extraction's correct pinyin.
